results.content: But while Republicans made notable gains among some minority voters in the 2024 presidential election, more recent polling suggests those gains should not be interpreted as a broad or continuing realignment toward the GOP. Yet by April 2026, approval of Trump among Hispanic voters who had supported him in 2024 had fallen to 66%, a 27-point decline from early 2025. Civiqs, a nonpartisan online polling firm that surveys presidential approval on a rolling basis, puts Trump's current approval in Idaho at 49 percent, with 41 percent disapproving as of Thursday. That figure has fluctuated near that line in recent weeks. The Idaho Democratic Party cited the same Civiqs data in a statement released Aug. 19. [...] The shift marks a significant change in a state Trump carried by more than 36 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election and where his approval stood well above 50 percent for most of his second term. Wyoming, North Dakota and West Virginia are currently the only other states where Trump holds a positive approval rating above 50 percent.
